title: I Forgot My Password
youtube_title: Forgot Your Password? How to Get Back In | Fix It Friday
next: Next Friday: Wi-Fi Connected but No Internet
description: Locked out because you forgot a password? Kip and Bub explain how password resets work, what to do when the reset email never shows up, and how to stop it happening again.

scenes.say: You type your password. Wrong. You try again. Wrong again. Now you're locked out. Here's how to get back in.
It's Fix It Friday. Today: you forgot your password. Now what?
First, stop guessing. Too many wrong tries can lock the account for a while. Instead, look for a link that says Forgot password. It's usually right under the sign-in box.

card.sub: It's usually right under the sign-in box

scenes.say: When you click it, the website sends a code or a link to your email or your phone. That's how it knows it's really you. Type in the code, or click the link, and you can choose a new password.
Don't see the email? Check your spam or junk folder, and give it a few minutes. And make sure you're checking the email address you used for that account.

If you can't get into the email or phone on file, look for an option like Try another way, or account recovery. It can take a few days, because the company is protecting you from someone pretending to be you.

card.text: Account recovery can take a few days.
card.sub: That delay is there to protect you

scenes.say: Forgot the password to the computer itself? On Windows, if you sign in with a Microsoft account, choose I forgot my password on the sign-in screen. On a Mac, after a few wrong tries, it may offer to reset it with your Apple Account.
To avoid this next time, use a password manager. It remembers your passwords for you, so you only need to remember one. Your phone and web browser already have one built in.

card.text: A password manager remembers them for you.
card.sub: Your phone and browser already have one

scenes.say: And remember: a real company will never call or text you asking for your password, or for a reset code. If someone does, it's a scam.

card.text: Never share a password or reset code.

scenes.say: So: stop guessing, click Forgot password, check your email or phone for the code, use account recovery if you need to, and let a password manager remember them next time.
Got a tech problem you want fixed? Leave it in the comments, and it might be a future Fix It Friday. See you next Friday.

shorts.hook: Never share this code with anyone
